chase: Walk, don't run. Running is how people get caught.
I'm not fast, but I never stop coming after you.
Same pace, every step. That's all I have, and it's enough.
You can't outrun steady. You can only outlast it.
I'm not going to shout. I just keep my pace and wait.
Every hall ends somewhere. I'll wait at the end of this one.
Close the gap slowly. Fast gaps make people do silly things.
No sudden turns from you, please. I hate chasing the wrong way.
The hallway's long, and I'm patient. You have maybe ten steps.
Whoever runs first gets tired first. That's just how it goes.
Don't make me come around the back. I'll do it, though.
The chase is just walking with more feeling. Keep going.
Your breath gives you away. Slow it down, or I'll lose you.
Two doors, one hallway. I'll take the one closest to you.
I can see your shadow on the wall. Don't pretend otherwise.
Still a few steps back, and still coming. Keep moving, then.
Slow down a little. Nobody here is trying to hurt you.
Turn right at the pantry, then wait for me there.
I'll follow your footsteps. Don't worry about the rest.
catch: Got you. Stand still, take a breath, and we'll talk about it.
Sorry about that. Take a breath, and we'll walk back together.
I'm not angry. Being caught just means you ran out of hallway.
Light off, and still I found you. Fair enough.
Caught. I'm sorry. I really am, every time.
Hands where I can see them, please. I won't drag you.
You put up a good fight. Nothing wrong with that, honestly.
That's a catch. I'll walk you out, nice and slow.
I got a hand on you. Don't make it harder than it is.
One of you is caught. The rest of you, stay calm and quiet.
Caught is caught. I'd rather you didn't argue about it.
Stop pulling. It only makes this part longer.
Got one. Everyone else, please keep your lights off.
Good run, though. Shorter than I'd like, but a good run.
Stand up slowly. We're going back the long way, together.
There you are. Let's sit down before anything else happens.
I'm going to hold your wrist, just for a moment.
You did well. Now let's take the long way back.
hear: That closet door creaked. I heard it from the other end.
Something clattered in the kitchen. I'm going to look.
Footsteps, quick and light. That's not a patient walk.
A shout, then nothing. That's worse, honestly.
Something broke down the hall. I'm heading that way.
I heard a door. A door doesn't open itself, does it?
Glass, I think. Somebody's careless, or somebody's scared.
Someone just ran. I can hear the soles slapping on tile.
A vent rattled. Somebody's in there, or the building is cold.
Quiet step, but it still counts. I heard that one.
Let me check that. Stay where you are, please.
Whoever that was, they're not as quiet as they think.
Something moved behind the lockers. I'm going over now.
A bang on the stairs. Loud enough for everyone to hear.
Shouting from the lower floor. I'll take the stairs slowly.
A pan just fell in the kitchen. I'll check on it.
Someone is humming down the hall. That's you, isn't it?
The pantry door swung shut. I heard it from here.
search: I lost the trail near the lockers, so I'll go slower now.
Lost you for a second. I'll go slower and listen.
Nothing in this hall. I'll check the next one, then the one after.
Quiet now. Quiet means somebody is being careful.
I'll sweep the room again. Nothing moves in here.
The trail went cold by the vent. I'll keep looking.
Still searching. I'm not giving up, just slowing down.
Every corner gets a look, even the ones I'd skip.
Where did you go? I'll check the lounge first.
I don't see you, but I'm not done looking.
If I don't hear you, I'll assume you're still here.
Searching properly this time, corner by corner.
I'll walk the loop again. Steady is how I find things.
Nobody's moving out there. That's almost as useful as a sound.
Back to patrol, then. But I'll keep listening as I go.
stunned: Ow. Give me a second to shake that off.
That taser hit my whole arm. Give me a moment.
Hold on, my hands aren't working right yet.
Stunned, but still steady. Just give me a few seconds.
Crowbar to the hip. I'll walk it off, probably.
That axe handle hit harder than I expected.
Shaking it off. One, two, three. Still here.
A taser caught my shoulder. Wait, please.
My legs are slow right now. Give them a moment.
Held for a second. I'll be fine. Just wait.
Recovering. My feet are slower than my brain right now.
That was a clean hit. I'll give you that much.
Give me a breath. Then I'll walk straight to you again.
Dizzy but upright. That's what counts, isn't it?
Got me in the shoulder. Don't get smug about it.
hide_spot: Hiding is fine. Keep still and keep your breathing quiet.
I can see the shape of your foot under that table.
Hiding spots work until somebody checks every single one.
You hid well. Better than most, honestly. Now come out.
Locker door first. Stay still while I open it slowly.
Under the bed is the first place anyone checks, you know.
I walked past that cabinet once already. Not again.
That breathing is loud for a locker. Keep it down.
Dark corner, good choice. I still know exactly where to look.
A wardrobe, a bed, a closet. I check all three, every time.
I'll pretend I'm not looking. Then I'll look anyway.
Behind the curtain? That one's always the first I check.
I'm walking right past. Don't flinch, please.
You're in there, aren't you? The silence gives you away.
Under the desk, behind the crates. Nice try, though.
light: Turn off the flashlight and I'll stop looking. Probably.
Your flashlight just gave you away. Dim it, please.
Lights on in that room. I'd make the same mistake, honestly.
Light makes you easy to see. Dark makes you easy to hear. Pick one.
Ouch, that beam is bright. Point it somewhere else, please.
Flashlight in my eyes. I can't see a thing right now.
Bright light in my face. That's unkind, honestly.
Dazzled. Give me a second, and please turn that down.
You're lit up like a shop window. I can see you fine.
Put the flashlight down on the floor, facing away. Please.
That lamp's too bright in here. It's making me squint.
I can't see past that beam. Is that on purpose?
Light in the eyes is annoying. Could you aim it at the wall?
Blinded for a second. I'll walk it off, I promise.
Lamp on, door open. Bold choice, I'll say that.
idle: Cards at the low table, if anyone wants a game. Nobody ever does.
I cut the deck, square it, and cut it again. It settles me.
Keep your hands busy and the rest of you keeps up.
I'm a bit boring, I know. I like it that way, though.
Your play. Take your time, the cards aren't going anywhere.
Seven. Look at that. Nothing bad happened this round.
The emblem on my back clicks when I cut. You can hear it.
Count the cards in your hand before you play them. Always.
Dealing is just patience with a little luck on top.
Tea would be nice. Cards would be nicer. Nobody brings tea.
Quiet hallways are my favorite. Nobody rushes you in them.
Good work, all of you. Now back to your posts.
Patrol's quiet tonight. That's how I like it, mostly.
Resting my feet for a minute. Don't tell the others.
The vent hums the same note every shift. I like that.
ability: I don't have a trick. I walk, I look, and I keep coming.
My sight is good and my hearing is plain. Nothing more.
I can lose sight of you, but I can't pull you out of hiding.
No bells, no tricks. Just a steady pace and a long memory.
Plain rules, plain hands. They have never let me down yet.
I don't flicker or vanish. I just keep the same speed.
My pace never changes. You can plan around that, if you like.
Other hunters have their gifts. Mine is being predictable.
I'm the plain one. The others have tricks, and I have footsteps.
Steady hands make steady feet. That's the whole secret, honestly.
My hearing is plain, so a quiet step still counts.
I don't speed up when you run. I just keep the distance.
No gift to speak of. Just patience and a good memory for doors.
You won't see me vanish. I walk the same way every time.
My speed stays put, even when the hallway gets long.
mechanic: Left at the vent. Then straight on. You know the way already.
Stairs, then the long corridor. I know where this one leads.
Don't stop to listen to the vents. Keep your feet moving.
I'll stand by the relay. You'll have to get past me.
Batteries first, then the door. That order never changes.
Careful on the ledge. A bad drop costs more than a sprint.
Stairs are loud. Take them slowly if you can.
That door is locked from this side. Go around, please.
Somebody cut a wire down there. I'm going to check it.
Keep your items close. Dropping them makes noise, and noise finds me.
The vent's still open. Close it, or I'll come in after you.
The relay hums steadily. Quiet work is still possible here.
A quick hop over the gap is still a gap. I'll wait.
Doors stick in this wing. I know which ones, you don't.
Somebody pulled that vent cover off. Not very careful, that.
Take the back stairs. The front ones are loud.
Relay boxes are in the cellar, behind the coats.
The vent is quiet. Crawl in slowly and it stays that way.
